key_insight: A DFT-informed all-atom model reproduces key experimental features of the resorcinol-formaldehyde aerogel skeleton and enables atomistic study of iron incorporation.
engineering_relevance: The model offers a starting point for screening fillers and dopants in RF aerogels for potential thermal-insulation and thermoelectric applications.
method: Optimize RF base units with DFT and compare calculated infrared spectra with experiment.
Benchmark classical force fields against DFT and select COMPASS II for a 15,012-atom skeleton model.
Equilibrate with NVT/NPT molecular dynamics, then simulate 5 wt% iron incorporation for 1 ns.
evidence_signal: The calculated infrared spectrum agreed with experiment, the equilibrium skeletal density was 1.296 versus 1.3 g/cm³ experimentally, and the embedded iron fraction increased from 63% to 71%.
watch_item: The branched RF units were not cross-linked to one another, and the simulations do not establish long-term dopant stability or thermal and thermoelectric performance.
paper_title: An All-Atom Model of the Resorcinol-Formaldehyde Aerogel Skeleton from DFT and Molecular Dynamics: Validation and Iron Incorporation
